subject: Audit harvest & handoff delivery options for Acme Bank

Cc: Acme Bank Legal <legal@acmebank.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: harvest & delivery options for audit/history

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team has followed up with a narrow ask: we need an operational playbook for extracting a full chronological history (audit events + request metadata + user identifiers) for a defined tenant for the last 36 months. Key acceptance criteria: integrity/tamper evidence, manifest with sequence numbers, and a delivery mechanism that supports encrypted bulk transfer to our S3.

Can you outline the delivery options (on-demand snapshot, continuous daily exports, and a retained query interface), expected SLAs for export completion for up to 10TB, redaction options prior to handoff, and any proofs of integrity (hash manifests, signed timestamps)? Also please point us to any sample delivery artifacts/format spec.

We are starting the procurement timeline next week and will need this for the RFP response.

Thanks,
Audrey Clarke
Director, Compliance
Acme Bank

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: harvest & delivery options for audit/history

Hi Audrey — thanks for the clear list. High-level options we recommend:

1) On-demand forensic snapshot (point-in-time): we produce a consistent export package (NDJSON event stream + metadata manifest + signed hash tree) and deliver via customer-managed S3 or secure transfer. Typical throughput: up to 10TB delivered within 48 hours with reserved Dedicated capacity; otherwise standard windows apply.

2) Scheduled bulk exports: daily or weekly deltas pushed to your S3 bucket (encrypted SSE-KMS), with sequence manifests for incremental replay.

3) Live query/read-only access: a time-bounded query API that streams a filtered event set (useful for narrow-scope investigations, lower transfer volumes).

Redaction: we support configurable redaction at export time (PII tokenization, field-level suppression, and deterministic pseudonymization). Integrity: each package includes a manifest.csv with per-file SHA256, a root signed timestamp (RFC 3161 style), and optional third-party notarization.

I attached a short handoff spec and a sample snapshot checklist to illustrate formats.

Next steps: Kimberly can confirm the export schema and quantify timing estimates for 10TB under Dedicated and Hosted modes. Marissa will surface any billing/commit implications for reserved export windows. If that works, we can prepare a concise RFP appendix tailored to your procurement template.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-handoff-spec.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Audrey Clarke <audrey.clarke@acmebank.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: harvest & delivery options for audit/history

Audrey — quick technical clarifications on formats and retention windows so we size correctly: 

- Export format: event-level NDJSON (one JSON object per line) for audit events; separate CSV manifest with SHA256 hashes and sequence offsets. We include a mapping file for internal field names and a schema.json for validation.
- Included data: per-event timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, user_id (pseudonymized on request), request_id, operation, resource_path, input_length, response_status, and model_version.
- Retention windows: hosted customers get default 30–90 days for verbose telemetry; we support contractual retention for 36 months under Dedicated/Private plans (with applicable fees).
- Throughput/backfill: For a full 36-month harvest ~8–12TB for a mid-volume tenant; with Dedicated reserved capacity we can prioritize export and target 24–36 hour completion for up to 10TB. Without reserved capacity, exports are queued subject to workload (typical 3–7 days).

I'll follow up with a sample schema snippet and an export timeline table.

—Kimberly
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Audrey — attaching a draft SOW language and delivery checklist that we've used with other banks. It includes acceptance tests (manifest integrity, sample record verification, delivery to your S3 with SSE-KMS), timing estimates, and optional notarization add-on.

Key commercial notes: prioritized export windows for full-harvest (<=48h for up to 10TB) require a short-term reserved capacity booking (we can offer a 2-week reserved slot as an add-on). Otherwise standard export SLA is best-effort with an estimated 3–7 day completion.

Attached: snapshot-checklist.pdf and draft-sow-acme.docx. Let us know if legal wants any changes; we can produce a redline-ready appendix for your procurement team.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple of asks from legal/procurement:

- Confirm that pseudonymization is reversible by Acme only (i.e., we hold the mapping keys) and provide the key custody model.
- Provide a concise pricing line for the 2-week prioritized export slot.

If you can put the redline-ready appendix and the sample manifest in our shared Drive link by EOD Thursday, procurement can slot this into the RFP. Appreciate it.

Best regards,
Audrey
